arxiv-2111-04855.title: Stability and bifurcations of symmetric tops
arxiv-2111-04855.creator: Eugene Lerman
arxiv-2111-04855.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Eugene Lerman. We study the stability and bifurcation of relative equilibria of a particle on the Lie group S ​ O ​ ( 3 ) SO(3) whose motion is governed by an S ​ O ​ ( 3 ) × S ​ O ​ ( 2 ) SO(3)\times SO(2) invariant metric and an S ​ O ​ ( 2 ) × S ​ O ​ ( 2 ) SO(2)\times SO(2) invariant potential.

arxiv-2112-06007.title: Determinantal point processes based on orthogonal polynomials for sampling minibatches in SGD
arxiv-2112-06007.creator: Rémi Bardenet, Subhroshekhar Ghosh, Meixia Lin
arxiv-2112-06007.description: Abstract Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is a cornerstone of machine learning. When the number N N of data items is large, SGD relies on constructing an unbiased estimator of the gradient of the empirical risk using a small subset of the original dataset, called a minibatch.

arxiv-2207-14690.title: Renting Edge Computing Resources for Service Hosting
arxiv-2207-14690.creator: Aadesh Madnaik, Sharayu Moharir, Nikhil Karamchandani
arxiv-2207-14690.description: Abstract We consider the setting where a service is hosted on a third-party edge server deployed close to the users and a cloud server at a greater distance from the users. Due to the proximity of the edge servers to the users, requests can be served at the edge with low latency.

arxiv-2210-13206.title: Post-Selection Confidence Bounds for Prediction Performance
arxiv-2210-13206.creator: Pascal Rink, Werner Brannath
arxiv-2210-13206.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Pascal Rink, Werner Brannath. In machine learning, the selection of a promising model from a potentially large number of competing models and the assessment of its generalization performance are critical tasks that need careful consideration. Typically, model selection and evaluation are strictly separated endeavors, splitting the sample at hand into a training, validation, and evaluation set, and only compute a single confidence interval for the prediction performance of the final selected model.

arxiv-2306-12380.title: On the Validation of Gibbs Algorithms: Training Datasets, Test Datasets and their Aggregation Thanks: This work is supported by the Inria Exploratory Action – Information and Decision Making (AEx IDEM) and in part by a grant from the C3.ai Digital Transformation Institute.
arxiv-2306-12380.creator: Samir M. Perlaza 1 2 3 , Iñaki Esnaola 2 4 , Gaetan Bisson 3 , and H. Vincent Poor 2
arxiv-2306-12380.description: Abstract The dependence on training data of the Gibbs algorithm (GA) is analytically characterized. By adopting the expected empirical risk as the performance metric, the sensitivity of the GA is obtained in closed form. In this case, sensitivity is the performance difference with respect to an arbitrary alternative algorithm.

arxiv-2406-16516.title: Demonstration of a Squeezed Light Source on Thin-Film Lithium Niobate with Modal Phase Matching Journal: opticajournal
arxiv-2406-16516.creator: Tummas Napoleon Arge, Seongmin Jo, Huy Quang Nguyen, Francesco Lenzini, Emma Lomonte, Jens Arnbak Holbøll Nielsen, Renato R. Domeneguetti, Jonas Schou Neergaard-Nielsen, Wolfram Pernice, Tobias Gehring, Ulrik Lund Andersen
arxiv-2406-16516.description: Abstract Squeezed states are essential for continuous variable (CV) quantum information processing, with wide-ranging applications in computing, sensing and communications. Integrated photonic circuits provide a scalable, convenient platform for building large CV circuits. Thin-film Lithium Niobate (TFLN) is particularly promising due to its low propagation loss, efficient parametric down conversion, and fast electro-optical modulation.

arxiv-2508-21805.creator: Chirag Chawla, Sourav Chatterjee, Katelyn Breivik
arxiv-2508-21805.description: Abstract With its third data release (DR3), Gaia begins unveiling dormant candidate compact object (CO) binaries with luminous companions (LC) as predicted by several past theoretical studies. To date, 3 black hole (BH), 21 neutron star (NS), and ≈ 3200 \approx 3200 white dwarf (WD) candidates have been identified with LCs in detached orbits using astrometry.

arxiv-2510-21020.title: From Information to Generative Exponent: Learning Rate Induces Phase Transitions in SGD
arxiv-2510-21020.creator: Konstantinos Christopher Tsiolis, Alireza Mousavi-Hosseini, Murat A. Erdogdu
arxiv-2510-21020.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Konstantinos Christopher Tsiolis, Alireza Mousavi-Hosseini, Murat A. Erdogdu. To understand feature learning dynamics in neural networks, recent theoretical works have focused on gradient-based learning of Gaussian single-index models, where the label is a nonlinear function of a latent one-dimensional projection of the input.

arxiv-2512-08197.title: Integrating Delay-Absorption Capability into Flight Departure Delay Prediction
arxiv-2512-08197.creator: Jianyang Zhou
arxiv-2512-08197.description: Abstract Accurately forecasting flight departure delays is essential for improving operational efficiency and mitigating the cascading disruptions that propagate through tightly coupled aircraft rotations. Traditional machine learning approaches often treat upstream delays as static variables, overlooking the dynamic recovery processes that determine whether a delay is absorbed or transmitted to subsequent legs.

britannica-1911-oleic-acid.description: Article 'Oleic Acid' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 20), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. treated with hydrochloric acid, the lead chloride filtered off, the liquid concentrated, and finally distilled under diminished pressure. Oleic acid is a colourless, odourless solid, melting at 14° and boiling at 223° (10 mm.). On exposure it turns yellow, becoming rancid. Nitric acid oxidizes it to all the fatty acids from acetic to capric.

uslaw-usc-t10-s14309.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s14309.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part III (Promotion And Retention Of Officers On The Reserve Active-Status List); Chapter 1405 (Promotions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Acceptance.— An officer who is appointed to a higher grade under this chapter shall be considered to have accepted the appointment on the date on which the appointment is made unless the officer expressly.
